fixes.explanation: Close, because it does sound like the kind of thing a person would want. But in Luke 13:24 Jesus doesn't say wide and He doesn't say gate. His words are “…the narrow door.” That word narrow comes right after He says, “Make every effort…”

The Beautiful Gate is a real place, a temple gate where a man who was lame from birth was set down every day to beg (Acts 3:2). But it isn't in this passage. Here Jesus says to make every effort to enter through “…the narrow door.” Nice name, different building.
Evildoers is the word, baker. The master says, “Depart from me, all you evildoers.” It's a heavy line. The knocking in verse 25 ends with this answer.

Hypocrites is a word that fits in other places, but it isn't the one here. The people at the door point out that they ate and drank with him and that he taught in their streets (Luke 13:26). He still answers, “…Depart from me, all you evildoers.” The word he uses is evildoers.

That's a word that sounds right in a sermon, but it's not what the master says. The people at the door talk about eating and drinking with him, and about his teaching in their streets (Luke 13:26). His reply is, “…Depart from me, all you evildoers.” The word he picks is evildoers.

Yes! Jesus says they will see “…Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and all the prophets in the kingdom of God…” They see those faces while they themselves are thrown out. I think the weeping hits harder because those faces are right there in front of them.

Moses, Israel's leader (Exodus 3:10), is a great name to have on a list, and you're in good company thinking of him. But this isn't the list Jesus gives. In Luke 13:28 He says the ones thrown out will see “…Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and all the prophets…” The prophets are in there, but the priests aren't.

David, Israel's king (2 Samuel 5:3), would be a fine guest at any table, so I see the thinking. But that's not the lineup in verse 28. Jesus says they will see “…Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and all the prophets…” He names prophets, and He doesn't mention kings.

Galilee is a good guess, since Jesus went throughout it teaching (Matthew 4:23). But Luke 13:29 doesn't name a region at all. It says, “People will come from east and west and north and south…” The answer is all four directions.

Jesus did teach His disciples (Matthew 5:1-2), but that's not what He sends to the fox. In Luke 13:32 He says, “…I will keep driving out demons and healing people today and tomorrow…” Nothing in His message is secret. Quiet isn't the plan.

I can see why hiding sounds like a reaction to a threat. But Jesus doesn't say that. His message is, “…I will keep driving out demons and healing people today and tomorrow…” He adds, “Nevertheless, I must keep going today and tomorrow and the next day…”

A shepherd is a picture Jesus uses in other places (Luke 15:4), so I get why it came to mind. But in Luke 13:34 the picture is different. He says it's “…as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings…” This time it's a hen.

Nets and boats show up in the Gospels (Luke 5:4-7), so that's a natural guess. But it's not the picture here. Jesus says He longed to gather them “…as a hen gathers her chicks under her wings…” It's a hen and her chicks, not fishing gear.
